keyword: has there ever been a perfect bracket
claims: There has never been a publicly verified perfect NCAA March Madness bracket in history.
The odds of picking all 63 games correctly are estimated at 1 in 9.2 quintillion for random picks.
The odds of picking all 63 games correctly are estimated at 1 in 120 billion with basketball knowledge.
The longest verified streak is 49 consecutive correct games in 2019.
The longest known perfect streak belongs to Gregg Nigl.
Gregg Nigl correctly picked 49 consecutive games, lasting through the first two rounds and into the Sweet 16.
The odds of a perfect bracket are less likely than winning the Powerball jackpot three times.
Even if you filled out a bracket every second, it would take about 3,800 years to get one right.
The best streak in recent years was 42 games in 2024.
In 2025, over 280,000 entries got all four Final Four teams correct.
